Time2Route:
Build the route worth taking

A map-first route planner for walking and cycling. Build a route, discover interesting places nearby, add stops, read elevation, and share the result.

Written byVadim Markelov

Not just A to B — Build the route worth taking

Time2Route combines route planning, interesting places, stops, elevation profiles, and shareable links — all built around your route.

S Start
M Mode
1 Places
2 Stops
3 Elevation
D Destination

Your route, planned your way

Every route is a sequence of decisions. Here is how Time2Route turns a direction into a journey.

Choose start and finish Set where the route begins and where it should end.
Pick a travel mode Switch between walking and cycling before building the route.
Build the route Press the button and Time2Route draws the route on the map.

Start screen — set endpoints, pick a mode, and build the route.

Using the search bar, you can quickly find the place you need and set a route for it in a couple of clicks.

Walk or bike — different route, different feel

Time2Route supports two movement modes. When you switch the mode, your route will adjust to your type of movement and select interesting places nearby.

Walking vs cycling — same start/end, different route.

Interesting places near the route line

Time2Route finds interesting places in relation to the route you just built — not as scattered city-wide pins. Landmarks along the way, parks that make the walk feel more pleasant, viewpoints close enough for a short detour. The route is the filter, so discovery stays tied to the journey you are actually taking.

Stops on the route

Stopping turns the direction into a plan. Visit the observation deck, enjoy birdsong in the park, visit the outstanding museum — the route is recalculated around each stop.

Start → Destination
→
Start → viewpoint → park → museum → Destination

Elevation that is easy to read

Distance and duration tell you how long. Elevation tells you how it will feel. One glance at the profile and you know where the effort is.

Avoid surprise climbs
See steep sections before you start — no hidden hills mid-route.
Choose scenic effort
A climb to a viewpoint looks different from a climb through a tunnel. Pick the one worth it.
Understand the route before you go
Total ascent, max grade, rolling vs punchy — the profile tells the story in one glance.
